lines.text: Sir, your glove.

lines.plainText: Why then this may be yours for this is but one

lines.plainText: Your worship sir or else I mistook

lines.text: Well, you'll still be too forward.

lines.text: And yet I was last chidden for being too slow.
lines.plainText: And yet I was last chidden for being too slow

lines.text: Go to, sir. Tell me, do you know Madam Silvia?

lines.text: She that your worship loves?

lines.text: Why, how know you that I am in love?

lines.text: Marry, by these special marks: first, you have learned, like Sir Proteus, to wreathe your arms like a malcontent; to relish a love-song, like a robin redbreast; to walk alone, like one that had the pestilence; to sigh, like a schoolboy that had lost his ABC; to weep, like a young wench that had buried her grandam; to fast, like one that takes diet; to watch, like one that fears robbing; to speak puling, like a beggar at Hallowmas. You were wont, when you laughed, to crow like a cock; when you walked, to walk like one of the lions; when you fasted, it was presently after dinner; when you looked sadly, it was for want of money. And now you are metamorphosed with a mistress, that, when I look on you, I can hardly think you my master.
lines.plainText: Marry by these special marks first you have learned like Sir Proteus to wreathe your arms like a malcontent to relish a lovesong like a robin redbreast to walk alone like one that had the pestilence to sigh like a schoolboy that had lost his ABC to weep like a young wench that had buried her grandam to fast like one that takes diet to watch like one that fears robbing to speak puling like a beggar at Hallowmas You were wont when you laughed to crow like a cock when you walked to walk like one of the lions when you fasted it was presently after dinner when you looked sadly it was for want of money And now you are metamorphosed with a mistress that when I look on you I can hardly think you my master

lines.text: Are all these things perceived in me?
lines.plainText: Are all these things perceived in me

lines.text: They are all perceived without ye.
lines.plainText: They are all perceived without ye

lines.text: Without me? They cannot.
lines.plainText: Without me They cannot

lines.text: Without you? Nay, that's certain, for without you were so simple, none else would. But you are so without these follies, that these follies are within you, and shine through you like the water in an urinal, that not an eye that sees you but is a physician to comment on your malady.

lines.text: But tell me, dost thou know my lady Silvia?
lines.plainText: But tell me dost thou know my lady Silvia

lines.text: She that you gaze on so as she sits at supper?
lines.plainText: She that you gaze on so as she sits at supper

lines.plainText: Dost thou know her by my gazing on her and yet know'st her not

lines.text: What dost thou know?
lines.plainText: What dost thou know

lines.plainText: That she is not so fair as of you wellfavoured

lines.text: I mean that her beauty is exquisite but her favour infinite.
lines.plainText: I mean that her beauty is exquisite but her favour infinite

lines.text: That's because the one is painted, and the other out of all count.
lines.plainText: That's because the one is painted and the other out of all count

lines.text: How painted? And how out of count?
lines.plainText: How painted And how out of count

lines.text: Marry, sir, so painted to make her fair, that no man counts of her beauty.
lines.plainText: Marry sir so painted to make her fair that no man counts of her beauty

lines.text: How esteem'st thou me? I account of her beauty.
lines.plainText: How esteem'st thou me I account of her beauty

lines.plainText: You never saw her since she was deformed

lines.text: How long hath she been deformed?
lines.plainText: How long hath she been deformed

lines.plainText: Ever since you loved her

lines.plainText: I have loved her ever since I saw her and still I see her beautiful

lines.text: If you love her, you cannot see her.
lines.plainText: If you love her you cannot see her

lines.text: Why?
lines.plainText: Why

lines.text: Because Love is blind. O, that you had mine eyes, or your own eyes had the lights they were wont to have when you chid at Sir Proteus for going ungartered!
lines.plainText: Because Love is blind O that you had mine eyes or your own eyes had the lights they were wont to have when you chid at Sir Proteus for going ungartered

lines.text: What should I see then?
lines.plainText: What should I see then

lines.text: Your own present folly and her passing deformity; for he, being in love, could not see to garter his hose; and you, being in love, cannot see to put on your hose.
lines.plainText: Your own present folly and her passing deformity for he being in love could not see to garter his hose and you being in love cannot see to put on your hose

lines.text: Belike, boy, then you are in love, for last morning you could not see to wipe my shoes.
lines.plainText: Belike boy then you are in love for last morning you could not see to wipe my shoes

lines.text: True, sir, I was in love with my bed. I thank you, you swinged me for my love, which makes me the bolder to chide you for yours.

lines.plainText: In conclusion I stand affected to her

lines.plainText: Last night she enjoined me to write some lines to one she loves

lines.plainText: Unto the secret nameless friend of yours

lines.plainText: Which I was much unwilling to proceed in

lines.plainText: But for my duty to your ladyship

lines.plainText: I thank you gentle servant 'tis very clerkly done

lines.plainText: Now trust me madam it came hardly off

lines.plainText: For being ignorant to whom it goes
